- `den_criterion_needs_five`: the hypothesis `ℓ ≥ 5` is sharp (fails at `ℓ = 3`: `N = 8`, `P = (1,3)`, `x(2P) = −7/4`), and `three_dvd_den_double_iff` gives the *correct* law there: `3 ∣ den x(2P) ↔ 9 ∣ y`.
- `two_dvd_den_double_iff` / `sixteen_dvd_den_double`: for odd `N`, `2 ∣ den x(2P) ↔ 2 ∣ y`, and then `16 ∣ den x(2P)`. Together these classify **every** prime.
- `infinitely_many_N_with_good_prime`: for a fixed prime `ℓ ≥ 5`, infinitely many `N` (explicit family `N_m = ℓ²(m+1)² − 1`) admit such a point.

- `barrier_bad_primes_absent`, `factorisation_barrier`: the opposite barrier — for `N = 35 = 5·7`, `P = (1,6)`, `x(2P) = −31/16`, so neither prime factor of `N` appears in the denominator.

# Future directions

Derived from the Stage-3 analysis and Stage-4 critique of the "only bad primes" refutation
(`Catalog/Shared/MordellDenominatorPrimes.lean`,
`Catalog/Shared/MordellDenominatorValuations.lean`,
`Catalog/Shared/MordellDenominatorBarriers.lean`).

What is already settled: for a Mordell curve `E_N : y² = x³ + N`, an integral point `P = (x,y)`
with `y ≠ 0`, and a prime `ℓ ≥ 5` with `ℓ ∤ N`,

* `ℓ ∣ den x(2P) ⇔ ℓ ∣ y ⇔ 2P̄ = O in E_N(𝔽_ℓ)` (`dvd_den_double_iff`,
  `reduction_double_eq_zero`, `addOrderOf_reduction_eq_two`);
* quantitatively `v_ℓ(den x(2P)) = 2 v_ℓ(y)` (`pow_dvd_den_double_iff`);
* the two remaining primes are classified as well: for odd `N`, `2 ∣ den x(2P) ↔ 2 ∣ y` and
  then even `16 ∣ den x(2P)` (`two_dvd_den_double_iff`, `sixteen_dvd_den_double`); for
  `3 ∤ N`, `3 ∣ den x(2P) ↔ 9 ∣ y` (`three_dvd_den_double_iff`) — the criterion at `3` is the
  generic one shifted by exactly one level, which is why `5 ≤ ℓ` was needed
  (`den_criterion_needs_five`);
* the phenomenon occurs for every prime `ℓ ≥ 5` and, for each such `ℓ`, for infinitely many
  `N` (`good_prime_realised`, `good_denominator_primes_infinite`,
  `infinitely_many_N_with_good_prime`);
* conversely the prime factors of `N` may be entirely absent from `den x(2P)`
  (`factorisation_barrier`).

The following conjectures are the next targets.

---

## Conjecture 1 (`n`-fold valuation law / elliptic divisibility squares)

For an integral point `P = (x, y)` on `E_N`, a prime `ℓ ≥ 5` with `ℓ ∤ N`, and every `n ≥ 1`,

> `v_ℓ(den x(nP)) = 2 · v_ℓ(W_n)`, where `W_n` is the `n`-th term of the elliptic divisibility
> sequence attached to `(E_N, P)`; in particular `den x(nP)` is always a perfect square and
> `ℓ ∣ den x(nP)` iff `n` is a multiple of the order of `P̄` in `E_N(𝔽_ℓ)`.

**The key insight is** that the affine denominator is the square of a division-polynomial
value, so the entire denominator tower is controlled by a single divisibility sequence whose
`ℓ`-adic behaviour is the rank-of-apparition function of `E_N(𝔽_ℓ)`.

**Why now?** The `n = 2` case is now fully formalised, including the non-cancellation lemma
`not_dvd_double_num`, which is the only genuinely arithmetic input; the induction step needs
the addition formula for `x(P + Q)` already present in Mathlib's `Affine/Formula.lean`.
Falsifiable: a single `(N, P, n, ℓ)` with `v_ℓ(den x(nP))` odd would refute it.

## Conjecture 2 (density of good denominator primes for a fixed curve)

Fix `N` and an integral non-torsion point `P` on `E_N`.  Then

> the set `S(N,P) = { ℓ prime : ℓ ∣ den x(nP) for some n ≥ 1 }` has natural density `1` inside
> the primes of good reduction; equivalently, all but density-zero many good primes `ℓ` divide
> some denominator.

**The key insight is** that `ℓ ∈ S(N,P)` iff `P̄` is torsion in `E_N(𝔽_ℓ)`, which is automatic
because `E_N(𝔽_ℓ)` is finite — so the obstruction is only that the *first* `n` with
`nP̄ = O` might exceed the range examined; the content is a uniform effective bound
`n ≤ ℓ + 1 + 2√ℓ` from Hasse.

**Why now?** The equivalence "denominator ⇔ reduction to `O`" is proved here for `n = 2`;
Hasse's bound is available in Mathlib for the point count of elliptic curves over finite
fields, so the effective form is within reach without new analytic input.  Falsifiable by
exhibiting a good prime `ℓ` with `nP̄ ≠ O` for all `n ≤ ℓ + 1 + 2√ℓ`.

## Conjecture 3 (no factoring signal: an indistinguishability theorem)

> For every `B` there are two semiprimes `N₁ = p₁q₁`, `N₂ = p₂q₂` with distinct factorisations
> and points `P₁ ∈ E_{N₁}(ℚ)`, `P₂ ∈ E_{N₂}(ℚ)` such that `den x(2P₁) = den x(2P₂)` while
> `min(p₁,q₁) > B`; i.e. the denominator is a *blind* statistic for factorisation.

**The key insight is** that `den x(2P) = 4y²/gcd(x⁴−8Nx, 4y²)` depends on `N` only through the
numerator, and one may vary `N = y² − x³` while holding `y` fixed, so a single denominator
value is shared by an infinite family of curves with unrelated factorisations.

**Why now?** `infinitely_many_N_with_good_prime` already builds the required family
`N_m = ℓ²(m+1)² − 1` with fixed `y`; upgrading "infinitely many `N`" to "equal denominators
for two semiprime `N`" needs only a search for two semiprime members of the family plus the
existing valuation law.  Falsifiable: a proof that equal denominators force equal `N`.

## Conjecture 4 (a uniform level-shift law at all primes and all multiples)

The `n = 2` case now reads: `v_ℓ(den x(2P)) = 2 v_ℓ(y) − c_ℓ` with `c_ℓ = 0` for `ℓ ≥ 5`,
`c_3 = 2` and `c_2 = −2` (an *anti*-shift: two extra powers appear).  Conjecturally this is
the `n = 2` instance of a general law:

> For every integral point `P` on `E_N`, every prime `ℓ` with `ℓ ∤ N`, and every `n ≥ 1`,
> `v_ℓ(den x(nP)) = 2 (v_ℓ(W_n) + ε_ℓ(n))`, where `W_n` is the elliptic divisibility sequence
> of `(E_N, P)` and the correction `ε_ℓ(n)` is supported on `ℓ ∣ 6n` and depends only on
> `v_ℓ(n)` and `ℓ` — never on `N`, `x` or `y`.

**The key insight is** that the corrections come from the constants in the duplication and
addition formulae (`4`, `9`, `8N`), i.e. from the ramification of the multiplication-by-`n`
isogeny at primes dividing `6n`; they are universal constants of the formal group rather than
arithmetic of the individual curve.

**Why now?** The three constants `c_2 = −2`, `c_3 = 2`, `c_ℓ = 0` are now *proved* for
`n = 2` in `Catalog/Shared/MordellDenominatorValuations.lean`, which supplies both the base
case and the exact shape of the general statement; the induction needs only Mathlib's
existing addition formula.  Falsifiable by an `(N, P, n, ℓ)` for which
`v_ℓ(den x(nP)) − 2 v_ℓ(W_n)` depends on `N`.

## Conjecture 5 (Mordell rank versus denominator prime growth)

> Let `r = rank E_N(ℚ)`.  Then the counting function
> `π_{N}(T) = #{ℓ ≤ T : ℓ good, ℓ ∣ den x(2P) for some P in a fixed basis of E_N(ℚ)/tors}`
> satisfies `π_N(T) ≫_r T / log T` as soon as `r ≥ 1`, with an implied constant depending only
> on `r` and the heights of the basis points.

**The key insight is** that each basis point contributes the primes dividing its `y`-coordinate
and, by the doubling law, those primes reappear squared at every level of the denominator
tower; independent basis points contribute essentially disjoint prime sets by a height
argument.

**Why now?** The `ℓ ∣ y` characterisation makes the statement purely about prime factors of the
`y`-coordinates of points of bounded height, which is amenable to the Lang–Trotter style
counting already used for elliptic divisibility sequences.  Falsifiable by a rank-1 curve
whose denominator primes are provably sparse.
